Sudoku Multi-Stack Parity POC

One contract. Three languages. The same results.

One Gherkin feature file drives the same Sudoku solver in TypeScript, Python and C#. CI fails the build if any Stack runs a different set of scenarios, runs them with different step text, or fails one.

One tick per scenario, in feature-file order. Green passed. Red did not pass.

Every scenario, on every Stack

Open a technique to list its scenarios, then select a scenario to see its steps. Outline rows are kept apart, so the eight move-validation rows are eight executions, not one.

One step, three languages

The feature file is shared. Each Stack binds the step in its own framework, and the gate requires the step text each one ran to match exactly.

Measured, not estimated
What each Stack costs

      
Sums and percentiles of per-scenario step time from this run. The C# figures come from the Cucumber Messages output, the others from Cucumber JSON.

    

      

      

        
This run

        

        
Scenario times add up the step durations. They leave out process start-up, compilation and set-up. Stacks differ in how they run, so this shows what each costs, not which is better.

      

    

  


  

    
Proof the proof works
The gate fails when it should

      
A gate that never fails proves nothing. Every build plants a change in a copy of one Stack's results and runs the gate on it. If the gate does not fail, the page is not built. Pick a case, then replay it. The output is this build's own run of the real gate on a copy of the results.
